newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK bourse pegs quote confusion on technical glitch.
newsitem.headline: HK bourse pegs quote confusion on technical glitch.

text.p: Hong Kong's stock market was thrown into confusion on Thursday when the bourse's computer erroneously showed the blue-chip Hang Seng Index had opened more than 500 points off.
"The cash market was a bit chaotic at the open," said a broker with a U.S. house.

Figures on Teletext, the exchange's computer-based information system that supplies stock and index quotations as well as news from the exchange, showed the blue-chip index off about 515 points in the opening minutes of trade.
The exchange later revised the index's morning low to 12,960.81, down 228.79 points from the previous close.
Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas, said the wrong figures caused minor inconvenience at the open but that trade quickly returned to normal.
"All trades were done at correct prices," Mak said. "Only the historical information on the screen was wrong."

The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong advised members to ignore the index's previous closing price shown on its Teletext page due to a technical malfunction with its Automatic Order Matching and Execution System.

Alec Tsui, deputy chief executive of operation services at the exchange, said in a statement that subscribers should use the previous closing price shown in free text areas as the reference for calculating the opening quotation.
The exchange also said the All Ordinaries Index (AOI) shown on its index and turnover page was to be disregarded.
Henry Law, head of the exchange's public and commercial services department, said the problem was with the closing prices of the previous session shown on the Teletext page.
"The closing price displayed in the Previous Close column of each stock in the Teletext system was incorrect," he told Reuters.

Hang Seng Index Services Ltd, which calculates the Hang Seng Index based on prices provided by the exchange, said it could not confirm the opening figures. It said it would issue a statement later in the day.
